key_insight: Introducing spanwise mean-flow skew into a turbulent mixing layer changes the magnitudes of mean and turbulent quantities, but leaves the layer’s core self-similar behavior largely intact.
engineering_relevance: This provides a controlled experimental benchmark for predicting and designing three-dimensional free-shear flows where incoming streams are not parallel.
method: Added skew using turning vanes mounted near the splitter-plate trailing edge
Measured downstream flow evolution with cross-wire anemometry
Compared planar and skewed mixing-layer statistics under similarity scaling
evidence_signal: The skewed case showed systematic reductions in mean and turbulent quantities of up to about 40%, while similarity collapse, near-linear thickness growth, and near-Gaussian Reynolds-stress shapes were preserved.
watch_item: The results are experimental and geometry-specific, so the apparent invariance of mixing-layer structure should not be assumed to generalize to all 3D shear flows.
paper_title: Effects of mean flow skew on turbulent shear layers. Part II. Experimental investigation
